label: food characteristic
definition: A physical object quality which is born by food material.
Definition

label: raw
definition: A characteristic of organism material which has a biochemical composition that closely resembles its harvested or subsequent biologically aged state.
comment: The definition covers plant, animal and fungi material, and allows for drying before harvest, and allows for cleaning, cutting, storing or trimming after harvest as long as harvested biological state is maintained.

label: raw (not intact)
definition: A characteristic of organism material which has undergone comminution or meat tenderizing, but which is otherwise unprocessed.
comment: This is a peer of "raw", intended to catch the case where a material maintains nutritional characteristics despite certain kinds of processing which may affect other characteristics related to food safety, taste, etc.

label: food (raw)
definition: Food material which is raw.

label: fresh
definition: A characteristic of raw organism material which has not undergone significant deterioration or spoilage, and which has not been subjected to drying or freezing.

label: food (fresh)
definition: Raw food which is fresh.

label: decayed
definition: A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's decomposition into component parts.
comment: This also allows for chemical synthesis resulting from decomposition products.

definition: Definition

label: mass of liquid
definition: An object which is composed primarily of a liquid.

label: food (liquid)
parent: food material by characteristic|mass of liquid
definition: A state of matter between a solid and a gas, in which a substance has the capacity to flow and conforms to the shape of a container.

label: liquid, higher viscosity
definition: A liquid that flows slowly at room temperature.
comment: Destined for PATO

label: liquid, lower viscosity
definition: A liquid that flows very easily at room temperature.
comment: Destined for PATO

label: quality of a liquid
definition: A physical quality inhering in an entity exhibiting the physical characteristics of an amorphous (non-crystalline) form of matter between a gas and a solid that has a definite volume, but no definite shape.

label: viscous
definition: A viscosity quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having viscosity.

label: mass of semi-solid material
definition: A mass of environmental material which is between solid and liquid material.

label: mass of solid material
definition: An mass of environmental material which is composed primarily of a solid environmental material

label: quality of a solid
definition: A physical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's exhibiting the physical characteristics of an entity characterized by particles arranged such that their shape and volume are relatively stable.

label: material processing
definition: A completely executed planned process that intends to output material entities from input material entities

label: food material processing
definition: Material processing involving food materials.

label: process by mechanism
definition: A planned process which has one or more action specification parts in its plan specification that control a mechanism.
comment: A convenience class for organizing processes by their physical mechanism or digital algorithm. An action may be physical, like pushing a button or setting a dial, or may be about running some software.

label: process by objective
definition: A planned process which has one or more objective specification parts in its plan specification.
comment: Implicitly this process must have a part which can sense when its one or more objectives are complete, so that it can halt. Process objectives might be classed as primary, secondary or tertiary but that may be relative to the needs of a supply chain.

label: material processing by mechanism
definition: Material processing which has one or more action specifications in its plan specification.
comment: A plan specification may manipulate parameters [variables / dimensions] to create an environment in flux that transforms/changes/affects the materials

label: material processing by objective
definition: Material processing which has one or more objective specification parts in its plan specification.
comment: Ideally infer that the change a process achieves is intentional (incl. energy efficiency w/r/t another process).  E.g. if some process has in its modelling that a single material input is divided into two or more material outputs, this matches the material component separation process. Is this a side-effect or intentional main point?  The latter is an objective.

label: food treatment
definition: Used to specifically characterize a food product based on the treatment or processes applied to the product or any indexed ingredient. The processes include adding, substituting or removing components or modifying the food or component, e.g., through fermentation.
comment: LanguaL curation note: This term is for CLASSIFICATION ONLY; DO NOT USE term in indexing. Use a more precise narrower term.

label: food modification
definition: A food treatment process in which a food material's composition is changed in some mechanical or chemical way.
comment: LanguaL curation note: Used when the food product underwent mechanical, chemical or enzymatic modification that has affected the texture, flavor or other characteristic of the product.

label: physical/chemical modification
definition: A food modification where physical or chemical changes are effected in any food ingredient through a physical or non-enzymatic chemical process.

label: molecular mechanism by reaction type
definition: A molecular mechanism categorized by its reaction type.

label: covalent reaction
definition: A molecular mechanism by reaction type involving a covalent reaction.

label: non-covalent reaction
definition: A molecular mechanism by reaction type involving a non-covalent reaction.

label: molecular mechanism by spatial location
definition: A molecular mechanism categorized by the region in which reactions are taking place.

label: surface mechanism
definition: A molecular mechanism where reactions are occurring at some surface boundary.

label: bulk molecular mechanism
definition: A molecular mechanism where reactions are occurring throughout a mixture.

label: microorganism control
definition: A material processing involving the control of pathogenic or fermentation related microorganisms in material.

label: food microorganism control
definition: A microorganism control process involving food related microorganisms in food material.

label: microorganism growth enhancement
definition: A microorganism control process in which microorganism cell viability is enhanced.

label: microorganism growth retardation
definition: A microorganism control process in which microorganism cell viability is reduced.

label: microorganism killing
definition: A microorganism control process in which microorganisms are destroyed.
comment: If food material is involved, we could infer this is a subclass of food preservation.

label: sterilization
definition: A microorganism killing process in which all microorganisms are destroyed in an input material.
comment: If food material is involved, we could infer instances of this is a subclass of food preservation.

label: sterile (sensu material)
definition: A characteristic of a material entity indicating that it has undergone sterilization.
comment: DIFFERENT: PATO Sterile refers to bearer's ability to reproduce:" A fertility quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being incapable of initiating, sustaining, or supporting reproduction.

label: sterile material
definition: A material entity which is sterile.

label: food (sterile)
definition: Food material which is sterile.

label: microorganism removal
definition: A food microorganism control process in which food microorganisms are removed from food material.

label: filtration
definition: filtration is a process which separates components suspended in a fluid based on granularity properties relying on a filter device.

label: microorganism filtration
definition: A filtration process which removes microorganisms from an input material.

label: microorganism micro-filtration
definition: A microorganism filtration process that consists of separating components by using semipermeable membranes with pore sizes between 0.1 and 10 micrometers to remove suspended particles or microorganisms from a fluid.

label: microorganism ultra-filtration
definition: A microorganism filtration process that consists of separating particles from a fluid using a semipermeable membrane with pores of 1-100 nanometers.
comment: Some dairy product are ultrafiltrated in order to obtain a higher protein concentration and hereby, a thicker consistency or textture. LanguaL curation note: Used when a product is preservation by the use of ultra-filtration to remove undesirable micro organisms and molecules. Example: beer.

label: ultra high pressure sterilization
definition: The process of holding food at a high pressure, normally greater than 1000 bar, which leads to sterilization. Example: Fruit juice, jam.

label: preservation by electron accelerator radiation
definition: Treated by electron accelerator radiation, for example to kill insects in cereals.

label: microbial/enzymatic modification
definition: A food modification by microbial or enzymatic action which results in molecular changes in any food component.
comment: LanguaL curation note: If salt, sugar or other food additive is used to aid in the modification, index it by the appropriate term under *INGREDIENT ADDED*.

label: food preservation
definition: A food treatment which contributes to the prevention or retardation of microbial, enzymatic or oxidative spoilage and thus to the durability of food material.
comment: LanguaL curation notes:  - This term is for CLASSIFICATION ONLY; DO NOT USE term in indexing. Use a more precise narrower term. - Index all methods for which information is available, even if a corresponding descriptor has already been used in *H. TREATMENT APPLIED*. Preservation descriptors refer to the finished food as a whole with these exceptions: (1) if the components of a multi-component food, such as cream pie, are preservation by different methods, index all methods; (2)  if chemical preservatives are declared on the label, always index them even if it is known that the preservative was introduced through or is only present in a component or ingredient of the food; and (3) if the preservation method for an ingredient is declared on the label (such as brie cheese made from pasteurized milk) index it. Also use *INGREDIENT preservation by THERMAL PROCESSING* or *INGREDIENT preservation by IRRADIATION* when ingredients have been pasteurized, ultrapasteurized, sterilized or irradiated.

label: food (perishable)
definition: Food which has a perishable characteristic.

label: perishable
definition: A characteristic of food material which indicates that over time it will more likely decompose, or spoil or cause illness due to foodborne microorganisms, unless subjected to a food preservation process.
comment: Perishability is often linked to the water activity (or concentration) in food materials.

label: shelf stable
definition: A characteristic food material which indicates that from a food safety perspective it can be safely stored at room temperature.
comment: Some food materials such as milk need sterilization to be shelf stable; others are shelf stable due to their dehydrated state, such as dates or dried peas.

label: durable shelf life
definition: A characteristic of shelf stable food material which indicates that in addition to being safely storable, it maintains its quality and desired palatability, and fulfills any nutritional declarations it has, up to some date of minimum durability.
comment: The general discriptive dimension here is "durability".  Some food materials such as bread need packaging and/or additives in addition to preservatives to extend their durable life. Ambient temperature or humidity may ultimately affect extend durable life performance.

label: chemical food preservation
definition: Preservation by use of chemical to destroy, suppress or inhibit undesirable microorganisms or enzyme activity.

label: preservation by treatment with chemicals
definition: Preservation by immersing in or spraying with liquids (e.g., sulfite solutions) or surrounding with gases (e.g., ethylene oxide, propylene oxide or sulfur dioxide) to destroy undesirable microorganisms or inactivate enzymes. Diffusion and chemical reaction may create a residue in the food product that contributes to continuing preservation.

label: preservation by adding chemical preservative
definition: Preservation by adding chemical preservatives (e.g., sorbic acid, sodium benzoate, BHT, calcium proprionate) to suppress or inhibit undesirable microorganisms or enzyme activity.

label: preservation by adding acid
definition: Preservation by adding acids or salts to suppress or inhibit undesirable micro-organisms or enzyme activity.

label: preservation by adding inorganic acids or salts
term: preservation by adding inorganic acids or salts
definition: Preservation by adding inorganic acids or salts (e.g. SO2, H2SO4, KNO4, NaNO3).

label: preservation by adding organic acids or salts
term: preservation by adding organic acids or salts
definition: Preservation by adding organic acids or salts (e.g. lactic acid, acetic acid, salicylic acid).

label: preservation by adding antibiotics
definition: Preservation by adding antibiotics (e.g. nisin, tylosine, subtlin, bacitracin, chlorotetracyclin, oxytetracyclin) to kill micro organisms or stop their growth.

label: preservation by reducing water activity
definition: A food preservation process which lowers the water activity (relative humidity) of a food product by drying (water reduction) or by adding salt, sugar or other agents to the food.

label: preservation by adding sugar
definition: Preservation by adding sugar, sugar syrup or by partial inversion of disaccharides until the sugar concentration is high enough to prevent growth of microorganisms.

label: controlled atmosphere storage
definition: Storage of fruits and vegetables in an atmosphere in which the concentrations of oxygen, carbon dioxide (and often nitrogen) are different from those in air and at a low temperature. All three (four) factors are controlled at the desired levels in order to suppress the fruits' and vegetables' natural respiration.

label: preservation by storage in modified atmosphere
term: preservation by storage in modified atmosphere
definition: Preservation by storage in an atmosphere in which the concentrations of oxygen and carbon dioxide are different from those in air. This reduces microbial and enzymatic activity; often used commercially in conjunction with refrigeration (e.g., refrigerated rail cars) for fresh meat and produce.

label: inert atmosphere storage
definition: Preservation by storage in inert gases (e.g. nitrogen) to suppress or inhibit undesirable micro-organism growth, oxidation activity, etc.

label: vaccum storage
definition: Storing under reduced pressure (e.g. 1.3-2 kPa) in order to suppress or inhibit undesirable micro organism growth, oxidation activity, etc.

label: preservation by irradiation
definition: Preservation by the use of radiation to destroy or suppress undesirable microorganisms or enzyme activity.

label: food material preservation by irradiation
definition: A preservation by irradiation process applied to food material.
comment: LanguaL curation note: Used when an ingredient or a component of a food has been preservation by irradiation.

label: preservation by ionizing radiation
definition: The application of ionizing radiation to food with the objective of food preservation by irradiation, primarily by high energy electromagnetic waves or particles.

label: food ultraviolet irradiation
definition: TBD:

label: ultraviolet light exposed (sensu food)
definition: A characteristic of irradiated food material which indicates that it has been exposed to ultraviolet light.

label: surface pasteurization or disinfection by ultraviolet irradiation
term: surface pasteurization or disinfection by ultraviolet irradiation
definition: A preservation by irradiation process in which microorganisms are reduced or eliminated on or in material by exposure to ultraviolet irradiation.
comment: LanguaL curation note: Used when sufficient ultraviolet radiation is applied to destroy most pathogenic and spoilage organisms present on the surface or to inhibit sprouting of stored agricultural produce and destroy storage pests. When followed by refrigeration, also index *preservation by CHILLING*.

label: food sterilization by irradiation
parent: preservation by ionizing radiation|food ionizing irradiation
definition: A preservation by irradiation process in which microorganisms are reduced or eliminated on or in food material by exposure to ultraviolet irradiation.
comment: LanguaL curation note: Used for a food product that has been packed in a hermetically sealed container and rendered commercially sterile by ionizing radiation (e.g. 24-28 kGy).

label: food irradiation
definition: A physical/chemical modification in which a food product or component is irradiated for any purpose.
comment: There are three kinds of irradiation that can be applied to food: gamma, electron-beam, and X-ray

label: food (irradiated)
definition: Food material which has been irradiated.

label: irradiated (sensu food)
definition: A characteristic of food material which indicates that it has undergone food irradiation.
comment: Irradiation changes the biochemical constitution of some/many foods, so this kind of raw food is not necessarily a child of “raw”: “Some foods, such as dairy foods and eggs, cannot be irradiated because it causes changes in flavour or texture.” [https://www.betterhealth.vic.gov.au/health/healthyliving/food-irradiation]

label: food ionizing irradiation
definition: A food irradiation process in which ionizing irradiation is applied.

label: disinfection by irradiation
definition: LanguaL curation note: Used when sufficient radiation (e.g. 1-5 k gy) is applied to destroy pathogenic and food spoilage organisms. Example: spices. Radurised food should be stored in a cool and dry place.
comment: LanguaL curation note: Used when sufficient radiation (e.g. 1-5 k gy) is applied to destroy pathogenic and food spoilage organisms. Example: spices. Radurised food should be stored in a cool and dry place.

label: heat treatment food preservation
definition: Preservation by the use of high temperature for a time sufficient to reduce or destroy undesirable microorganisms and enzyme activity. [FDA CFSAN 1995]

label: preservation of food component by heat treatment
term: preservation of food component by heat treatment
definition: LanguaL curation note: Used when an ingredient or a component of a food has undergone preservation by pasteurization, ultrapasteurization or sterilization.
comment: LanguaL curation note: Used when an ingredient or a component of a food has undergone preservation by pasteurization, ultrapasteurization or sterilization.

label: food sterilization by heating
definition: LanguaL curation note: Used when the product is rendered commercially sterile by holding at high temperature before or after it is packed in a hermetically sealed container.
comment: LanguaL curation note: Used when the product is rendered commercially sterile by holding at high temperature before or after it is packed in a hermetically sealed container.

label: food sterilization at ultra high temperature (UHT)
parent: aseptic filling and sealing of food
term: food sterilization at ultra high temperature (UHT)

label: food sterilization after filling
definition: LanguaL curation note: Used when a food product was sterilized by holding at a high temperature after filling.
comment: LanguaL curation note: Used when a food product was sterilized by holding at a high temperature after filling.

label: food sterilization by hot filling and cooling
term: food sterilization by hot filling and cooling
definition: LanguaL curation note: Used when a sterile product is filled into a container at approximately 212 degrees F and cooled promptly after sealing.
comment: LanguaL curation note: Used when a sterile product is filled into a container at approximately 212 degrees F and cooled promptly after sealing.

label: food sterilization before filling
definition: LanguaL curation note: Used when a food product is sterilized by holding at a high temperature before filling; the container may be sterilized before or after filling.
comment: LanguaL curation note: Used when a food product is sterilized by holding at a high temperature before filling; the container may be sterilized before or after filling.

label: aseptic filling and sealing of food
term: aseptic filling and sealing of food
definition: LanguaL curation note: Used when a sterile product is filled in a sterile atmosphere into a sterile container. For further detail see 21 CFR 113.3(a).
comment: LanguaL curation note: Used when a sterile product is filled in a sterile atmosphere into a sterile container. For further detail see 21 CFR 113.3(a).

label: food sterilization by hot filling, held hot and cooling
term: food sterilization by hot filling, held hot and cooling
definition: LanguaL curation note: Used when a sterile product is filled into a container at approximately 212 degrees F., sealed, and held hot temporarily to complete processing before cooling.
comment: LanguaL curation note: Used when a sterile product is filled into a container at approximately 212 degrees F., sealed, and held hot temporarily to complete processing before cooling.

label: pasteurization
definition: A microorganism killing process which has the objective of reducing potential pathogenic microbes by an amount equivalent to Pasteur's process.

label: food (pasteurized)
definition: Food material which has been pasteurized.

label: pasteurized
definition: A characteristic of food material which indicates that it has been pasteurized.

label: pasteurization by irradiation
definition: A pasteurization process which employs ionizing radiation.
comment: LanguaL curation note: Used when sufficient radiation (e.g. 10 kGy) is applied to destroy most patho-genic and food spoilage organisms. Also index *preservation by CHILLING*.

label: pasteurization by heating
definition: LanguaL curation note: Used when the product is held at a temperature of 60-150 °C (140-300 °F) for a time sufficient to destroy most pathogenic and food spoilage organisms. When followed by refrigeration, also index *preservation by CHILLING*.
comment: LanguaL curation note: Used when the product is held at a temperature of 60-150 °C (140-300 °F) for a time sufficient to destroy most pathogenic and food spoilage organisms. When followed by refrigeration, also index *preservation by CHILLING*.

label: ultra pasteurization (UP) by heat
definition: When used to describe a dairy product, means that such product shall have been thermally processed at or above 138° C (280° C) for at least 2 seconds, either before or after packaging so as to produce a product that has extended shelf life under refrigerated conditions (21 CFR 131.3 (c)). Used to describe liquid egg products that also have been thermally processed, but at a different temperature than for milk products.  The egg product will have an extended shelf life under refrigerated conditions.

label: high temperature short time (HTST) pasteurization
definition: High Temperature Short Time (HTST) pasteurization is one of the most common methods of pasteurization , which uses metal plates and hot water to raise milk temperatures to at least 72° C (161° F) for not less than 15 seconds, followed by rapid cooling.

label: higher heat shorter time (HHST) pasteurization
definition: Higher Heat Shorter Time (HHST) is a process similar to HTST pasteurization, but it uses slightly different equipment and higher temperatures (83 - 127° C) for a shorter time.

label: ultra high temperature (UHT) pasteurization
definition: Typically involves heating milk or cream to 135° to 150° C (275° to 302° F) for 1 or 2 seconds. The milk is then packaged in sterile, hermetically-sealed (airtight) containers (aspetic filling) and can be stored without refrigeration for up to 90 days. After opening, spoilage times for UHT products are similar to those of conventionally pasteurized products.

label: filling conditions for pasteurization
definition: A pasteurization by heating process in which containers are pasteurized in preparation for a filling process.
comment: LanguaL curation note: This term is for CLASSIFICATION ONLY; DO NOT USE term in indexing. Use a more precise narrower term.

label: pasteurization by heat after filling
definition: Pasteurization by heat after food material has been sealed in a container.

label: pasteurization by heat before filling
definition: Pasteurization by heat before food material has been sealed in a container.

label: low-temperature-long-time (LTLT) pasteurization
definition: A pasteurization by heating process which uses low heat for a longer time to kill pathogenic bacteria.
comment: An example of LTLT is when milk is pasteurized at 63° C (145° F) for 30 minutes.

label: clotting enzyme addition
definition: LanguaL curation note: Used when a clotting enzyme is added to a food product at any level.
comment: LanguaL curation note: Used when a clotting enzyme is added to a food product at any level.

label: food fermentation
definition: A fermentation process in which either carbohydrates, proteins or fats are modified through microbial, enzymatic and/or other biological processes.

label: food (fermented)
definition: Food material which has been fermented.

label: fermented
definition: A characteristic of food material which indicates that it has undergone fermentation.

label: lactic acid fermentation
definition: A food fermentation process in which lactic acid bacteria (LAB) convert carbohydrates into energy and lactic acid.

label: normal alcohol fermentation
definition: Conventional alcoholic fermentation involves crushing the grapes to free the juice and pulp from the skin with yeast serving to convert sugar into ethanol.

label: wine secondary alcohol fermentation
definition: The secondary stage of a wine alcohol fermentation and aging process, which takes three to six months, in which the fermentation continues very slowly. The wine is kept under an airlock to protect the wine from oxidation.

label: interrupted alcohol fermentation by sulphur addition
term: interrupted alcohol fermentation by sulphur addition

label: single component food fermentation
definition: A food fermentation process in which significant amounts of one category of component - either carbohydrates, proteins or fats - is modified through microbial processes.
comment: LanguaL curation note: Used for products in which either carbohydrates, proteins or fats were modified through microbial processes. Enzymatic or other biological processes may also be involved. If two or more of these components are modified in significant amounts, index under *FERMENTED/MODIFIED, MULTIPLE COMPONENT*.

label: multi-component food fermentation
definition: A food fermentation process in which significant amounts of two or more components (i.e. carbohydrate and protein, carbohydrate and fat, protein and fat, or all three) are modified through microbial processes.
comment: Enzymatic or other biological processes may also be involved.

label: proteolytic fermentation
definition: A food fermentation process in which proteolytic bacteria participate in fermentation by generating protease enzymes which break down protiens in food material.

label: lipolytic fermentation
definition: A food fermentation process in which microorganisms secrete lipases to break down lipids into glycerol and free fatty acids.

label: lactic acid-other agent fermentation
definition: A food fermentation process in which carbohydrates are converted into energy and lactic acid by microbials other than lactic acid bacteria.

label: carbonation by fermentation
definition: A food fermentation process involving production of carbon dioxide which remains noticeable in the food material.

label: component substitution
definition: A material processing in which a component of a material is removed and replaced by another material.
comment: LanguaL curation note: Use the appropriate narrower term for a food product that was prepared from a natural food product by removing an endogeneous component and adding a component of the same class. Index the specific component added under *INGREDIENT ADDED*, regardless of its level.

label: fat substitution
definition: A component substition process in which endogenous fat is removed and fat from a different source is added.
example of use: fat substitution in egg substitute in which edogenous egg fat is replaced by vegetable oil.

definition: Definition

label: material energy modulation
definition: Material processing which involves a change in energy applied to or inherent in a material.

label: thermal energy modulation
definition: An energy modulation in which thermal energy (heat) is added to or removed from a material or its environment.

label: material (thermally processed)
definition: A material which has been subject to thermal energy modulation.

label: thermally treated
definition: A characteristic of a material that has undergone a thermal energy modulation process.

label: temperature control
definition: A thermal energy modulation in which a material or environment is artificially controlled to ensure its temperature falls within a specified range.
comment: syn temperature regulation

label: temperature
definition: A physical quality of the thermal energy of a system.

label: core temperature
definition: A temperature of the bearer’s core region.

label: surface temperature
definition: A temperature of the bearer’s outer layer.

label: ambient temperature
definition: A temperature which refers to the average kinetic energy of molecules in the air surrounding an object or within a particular area.
Definition

label: uncontrolled environment
definition: An environment which is not temperature or humidity controlled.

label: uncontrolled temperature
definition: A temperature characteristic of a material which is not subjected to a temperature control process.

label: controlled environment
definition: An environment which is temperature and humidity controlled.
comment: syn . regulated environment Using the word "controlled" here rather than "regulated" since regulated may imply not just mechanical but regulatory control.

label: controlled temperature
definition: A temperature characteristic of a bearer which is the output of a temperature regulation process.
comment: syn. controlled temperature

label: foodsafe freezing temperature
definition: A freezing temperature (of a bearer) which meets safe food storage standards.

label: water freezing temperature
definition: A temperature which is of water when it transitions from liquid to solid phase at 1 atm of pressure.
comment: The measurement context of 1 atmosphere of pressure roughly equates to pressure on Earth at sea-level.

label: chilling temperature
definition: A temperature which indicates that the bearer is below a cool temperature but above a freezing temperature

label: foodsafe chilling temperature
definition: A chilling temperature (of a bearer) which meets safe food storage standards.
comment: The bearer can be a food item or a refrigerator / cooler.

label: cold temperature
definition: A temperature which indicates that the bearer is below a cool temperature.
comment: This covers common language use of "cold" which includes sub-zero temperature.

label: cool temperature
definition: A temperature which indicates that the bearer is below room temperature but above a cold temperature.
comment: The range of "cool" vs. "cold" temperatures is fuzzy.

label: room temperature
definition: A temperature which encompasses the range of air temperatures most people find comfortable indoors while dressed in typical clothing.

label: ISO 1 standard temperature
definition: A reference temperature of 20 Degrees celcius which enables standardized comparison of material characteristics.

label: neutral temperature
definition: A temperature relative to a material entity at which it maintains its physical or chemical constitution over time, all other things considered.
comment: Fresh food material doesn't really have a neutral temperature since the conditions for being "fresh" are also the conditions for eventual decay.  A frozen material may have a neutral temperature range within which it won't change its composition appreciably.

label: warm temperature
definition: A temperature (of a bearer) which is greater than room temperature and less than a hot temperature.

label: hot temperature
definition: A temperature (of a bearer) which is greater than warm temperature.
comment: This may be subjectively relative to a material - hot oil vs hot water

label: skin burning temperature
definition: A temperature of a bearer which is capable of inflicting pain or injury to epithelial tissue due to thermal exposure by conduction or infrared radiation.
comment: This pertains to cooking implements that may pose a burn risk.

label: scalding temperature
definition: A skin burning temperature of a bearer which indicates the bearer is a liquid.

label: boiling point
definition: A temperature characteristic of a liquid at which the vapour pressure of the liquid equals the pressure surrounding the liquid and the liquid changes into a vapour.
comment: The boiling point of a liquid varies depending upon the surrounding environmental pressure.[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boiling_point]

label: water boiling point
definition: A boiling point characteristic of water
Definition

label: material cooling
definition: A thermal energy modulation in which heat is removed from a material or (indirectly) its environment.

label: cooling material to a threshold
definition: A material cooling process which commenses when a material is placed into an environment which has a cooler temperature.
comment: This definition is engineered to fit both refrigeration and "icewater soaking" or other food preparation processes.

label: material chilling
definition: A cooling material to a threshold process which is at or above the freezing point of water, and less than a cool (~7°C) temperature.
comment: The temperature range for cooling varies between 30°F and 45°F (-1°C and 7°C), depending on jurisdiction.

label: food (chilled)
definition: Food material which is the output of a cooling material to a threshold process.

label: food (foodsafe chilled)
definition: Chilled food which is within a recommended foodsafe chilling temperature.

label: chilled
definition: A chilling temperature characteristic of material indicating that it bears this temperature by having undergone a cooling material to a threshold process.

label: chilled fresh
definition: A chilled temperature of material which also holds a fresh characteristic.
comment: This doesn't necessarily imply that a food product is foodsafe chilled.

label: foodsafe chilled
definition: A characteristic of chilled food material that has a temperature which meets safe food storage standards.

label: refrigeration
parent: cooling material to a threshold|food preservation
definition: A cooling material to a threshold process which is carried out during short or long-term food storage.

label: refrigeration with a refrigerating agent
definition: A process of refrigeration involving a refrigerating agent.
comment: Refrigeration can be as complex as with compressors and gas, or as simple as with ice in a container.

label: food (refrigerated)
definition: Food material which has undergone refrigeration.
comment: This class doesn't commit to whether or not refrigerated food has been kept at a food safe temperature standard. Also, this term covers both cooked, reheated and uncooked (possibly fresh) food.

label: refrigerated
definition: A characteristic of food material which has undergone refrigeration and/or is within a refrigerator.
comment: One can say that food material is refrigerated, but this does not commit to the degree to which such material has become chilled or frozen.

label: material freezing
parent: cooling material to a threshold|food preservation
definition: A cooling material to a threshold which transition its phase from a liquid or gas into a solid.
comment: We commonly associate water with freezing, but dry ice is an example of gaseous carbon dioxide cooling under pressure and turning directly into solid carbon dioxide blocks. [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dry_ice]

label: food (frozen)
definition: Food material which has undergone freezing.
comment: Includes both meat, fish, and kinds of fruit and vegetable that freeze well.

label: frozen
definition: A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being kept below its freezing point.

label: food (fresh frozen)
definition: Food which has a fresh frozen characteristic.

label: fresh frozen
definition: A frozen characteristic which indicates the bearer (organism material) had a fresh or blanched state immediately before being frozen.
comment: syn “frozen fresh.”

label: frozen after cooking
definition: A characteristic of food material which was cooked and then frozen.

label: food natural freezing

label: drying
definition: A material component separation process in which water or another solvent is removed from a material.
example of use: - Ethyl acetate decaffeination - the solvent being removed is ethyl acetate, not water. Describing this step as “drying” is consistent with chemical usage, even though a food‑centric reader might implicitly associate drying with water removal. "decaffeinated" is the adjective - Citrus peel extraction using isopropyl alcohol - isopropyl alcohol is used as the extraction solvent, The alcohol is later evaporated from the extract. - Using rotatory vacuum driers or rotatory vacuum driers for non-water applications - dealcoholizing wine. "dealcoholized" adjective.

label: food material combination
definition: A material combination process involving two or more food materials.
comment: LanguaL curation note: A food product is characterized by its main ingredient (food source and part); the addition of secondary ingredients is considered a treatment applied to the product. Secondary ingredients are indexed according to rules that are based on the order of predominance by weight (not counting water) as seen from the label statement, formulation or recipe and/or from the amount of the ingredient as percentage of total product weight. The general rule is:  an ingredient is always indexed if it is the second ingredient in order of predominance, if it is used as a filling, or if it is part of the product name(e.g., raisin bread). Specific rules are given in the scope note for the individual ingredient added; these rules specify more exhaustive indexing. For example, *MUSHROOM ADDED* is indexed regardless of ingredient position. another specific rule is given in the scope note for *SALTED*:  Use if the level of salt is more than 4%. Such a rule is used only when the percentage level can be inferred from the list of ingredients.

label: food micro-encapsulation
definition: Micro-encapsulation is a process in which tiny particles or droplets are surrounded by a coating to give small capsules many useful properties. In a relatively simplistic form, a microcapsule is a small sphere with a uniform wall around it.
comment: The material inside the microcapsule is referred to as the core, internal phase, or fill, whereas the wall is sometimes called a shell, coating, or membrane. Most microcapsules have diameters between a few micrometers and a few millimeters. The definition has been expanded, and includes most foods. Every class of food ingredient has been encapsulated; flavors are the most common. The technique of microencapsulation depends on the physical and chemical properties of the material to be encapsulated.[http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micro-encapsulation]  LanguaL curation note: Used for the coating of microscopic particles with another material.

definition: A wine maceration process which occurs in a room temperature environment without other atmospheric controls.????

comment: Various techniques of thermo-maceration were developed on the basis of evolution of the industrial technologies. The extraction principle consists in heating the whole grapes or the crushed and destemmed grapes to high temperatures (65–80◦C), promoting the diffusion of phenolics from the skins, especially anthocyanins.[https://www.bio-conferences.org/articles/bioconf/full_html/2017/02/bioconf-oiv2017_02032]

comment: In the past, smoking was a useful preservation tool, in combination with other techniques, most commonly salt-curing or drying. For some long-smoked foods, the smoking time also served to dry the food. Drying, curing, or other techniques can render the interior of foods inhospitable to bacterial life, while the smoking gives the vulnerable exterior surfaces an extra layer of protection. [Wikipedia]|LanguaL curation note: Used when smoking is used for preservation.

label: ikajime
definition: An animal harvesting process in which a fish is slaughtered by insertion of a spike quickly and directly into the hindbrain, usually located slightly behind and above the eye, thereby causing immediate brain death, which enables the quality of the fishes' meat to be maintained.
comment: The technique originated in Japan, but is now in widespread use. [...] When spiked correctly, the fish fins flare and the fish relaxes, immediately ceasing all motion. Destroying the brain and the spinal cord of the fish will prevent reflex action from happening; such muscle movements would otherwise consume adenosine triphosphate (ATP) in the muscle, and as a result produce lactic acid and ammonia, making the fish sour, soggy and less tasteful. Furthermore, the blood contained in the fish flesh retracts to the gut cavity, which produces a better coloured and flavoured fillet, and prolongs shelf life. [Wikipedia]
